issues.legal_issue: The Limitation Act cannot be applied by implication to consumer complaints filed before a limitation period was prescribed under the consumer-protection legislation.
material_facts: The consumer complaint was filed before the enactment of the provision prescribing a two-year limitation period for consumer complaints.
At the time the complaint was filed, the consumer-protection legislation prescribed no limitation period for such complaints.
The Limitation Act had not been expressly made applicable to proceedings under the consumer-protection legislation.
issues.conclusion: The Limitation Act did not apply by implication to the complaint, and the complaint could not be dismissed as time-barred under that Act.
issues.legal_principle: Section 24A of the Consumer Protection Act, inserted with effect from 18 June 1993, first prescribed a limitation period for complaints and allowed delay to be condoned for sufficient cause by recorded reasons. Sections 2(j) and the definition of a prescribed period in the Limitation Act concern periods prescribed for suits, appeals, and applications; a consumer complaint is not one of those proceedings. Where the legislature had not prescribed a limitation period for consumer complaints, courts could not import the Limitation Act by implication. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. B.N. Sainani was distinguished: it did not approve applying the Limitation Act to such complaints.

predicates.consumer_complaint: A consumer brings a complaint before a consumer dispute-resolution body.
predicates.filed_before_consumer_limitation_period_: The complaint was filed at a time when the governing consumer legislation did not prescribe a limitation period for complaints.

issues.definition: When a consumer complaint is filed before the governing legislation prescribes a limitation period for such complaints, the Limitation Act is not applied to it by implication.

issues.legal_issue: A specific-performance consumer complaint is timely under the applicable limitation period where no time for performance was agreed, the promisor continued to acknowledge liability until a later notice, and the complaint was filed within three years of that notice.
material_facts: The complaint sought enforcement of an agreement to sell a flat, and the parties had specified no period for specific performance.
The appellants had not denied their liability to execute the sale deed and had acknowledged liability to deliver legal possession up to 30 August 1991.

In a notice dated 30 August 1991, the appellants demanded a disputed balance and required the respondent to take legal possession, after which the respondent could at the latest assume that they were not interested in performing the agreement.
The complaint was filed on 19 June 1992, within three years of that notice.
issues.conclusion: Even assuming the Limitation Act applied, the complaint was within time when measured from the date on which the respondent could at the latest treat the appellants as unwilling to perform the agreement.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied Article 54 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act, under which the limitation period for specific performance runs from the date fixed for performance or, where no date is fixed, when the plaintiff has notice that performance is refused. Because no performance date had been agreed and liability continued to be acknowledged, the Court treated the notice of 30 August 1991 as the latest date from which the period could run. The Court made this alternative finding without holding that the Limitation Act applied to consumer complaints.

rule.if: consumer_complaint and specific_performance_claim and no_agreed_performance_deadline and liability_acknowledged_until_later_notice and complaint_within_three_years_of_notice

predicates.consumer_complaint: A consumer brings a complaint before a consumer dispute-resolution body.
predicates.specific_performance_claim: The consumer seeks enforcement of an agreement to transfer property.
predicates.no_agreed_performance_deadline: The parties did not fix a date or period for performance of the agreement.
predicates.liability_acknowledged_until_later_notic: The party required to perform continued to acknowledge its liability until a later communication that could alert the claimant to its unwillingness to perform.
predicates.complaint_within_three_years_of_notice: The claimant filed the complaint within three years after the communication that could alert the claimant to the refusal to perform.

issues.definition: A specific-performance consumer complaint is timely, on the assumed application of the relevant limitation period, when no performance deadline was agreed, liability was acknowledged until a later notice, and the complaint followed within three years of that notice.

issues.legal_issue: An order for specific performance need not be disturbed merely because the promisor alleges an unpaid balance where the consumer’s assertion that the consideration was paid was not denied and the reviewing bodies found no jurisdictional error or material irregularity.
material_facts: The respondent stated that the agreed consideration had been paid, and that assertion was not denied by the appellants.
The appellants asserted that a balance remained payable; the respondent claimed compensation for expenses incurred to repair the substandard flat.
The State Commission directed specific performance, and the National Commission found no jurisdictional error or material irregularity warranting interference.
issues.conclusion: The alleged unpaid balance did not justify setting aside the specific-performance direction, and the findings and orders of the consumer commissions required no interference.
issues.legal_principle: The Court relied on the factual findings made by the State Commission and accepted the National Commission’s conclusion that no jurisdictional error or material irregularity justified interference. It found no substance in the argument that the alleged balance defeated the relief, given the uncontroverted assertion that the consideration had been paid and the respondent’s claim concerning repair expenses. No statutory provision or earlier case was cited for this aspect of the decision.

rule.if: consumer_specific_performance_proceeding and payment_assertion_not_denied and alleged_balance_disputed_by_repair_claim and reviewing_body_found_no_jurisdictional_error_or_material_irregularity

predicates.consumer_specific_performance_proceeding: A consumer seeks specific performance of an agreement through consumer dispute-resolution proceedings.
predicates.payment_assertion_not_denied: The consumer asserts that the agreed consideration was paid, and the opposing party does not deny that assertion.
predicates.alleged_balance_disputed_by_repair_claim: The opposing party alleges that a balance remains payable, while the consumer claims expenses or compensation relating to defects in the property.
predicates.reviewing_body_found_no_jurisdictional_e: The reviewing body finds no jurisdictional error or material irregularity warranting interference with the order under review.

issues.definition: Where a consumer seeks specific performance, the payment assertion is not denied, an alleged balance is disputed by a repair claim, and the reviewing body finds no jurisdictional error or material irregularity, the specific-performance direction is not disturbed.
